summary: Backend-only regression testing of the Flutterwave inbound webhook signature guard (POST /api/webhook and POST /api/failed_webhook) against the preview host. Created 10 pytest cases (missing header, wrong header, empty header, malformed body, repeated bad requests, health check) - ALL 10 PASS. Verified via backend logs that the unsigned payload is now rejected BEFORE any processing and no ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT/'headers already sent' error occurs. IMPORTANT: on the first run the running ts-node process was STALE (started 03:19, webhooks/index.ts edited 03:23; ts-node has no hot reload) and still executed the old buggy path - logs showed 'here==========>' + 'IWebHook=============>' and a setRedisItem write for an unsigned 401'd payload. After `supervisorctl restart backend`, the fixed code loaded and post-401 processing lines disappeared entirely.

minor.issue: Pre-restart (stale ts-node process) the unsigned payload was still processed and wrote a junk Redis key 'flw-txt-TEST_flw-txt-qa-invalid-sig' on the LIVE Redis (from my rejected test payload). Consider deleting that key. Root cause of the stale behaviour: backend runs `ts-node --transpile-only server.ts` with NO hot reload, so any backend TS edit requires `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` before it takes effect (self-checks can otherwise validate old code).

Health endpoint is mounted on the express app root (server.ts L366), not under /api, so it is unreachable through the public preview host (non-/api paths route to Next -> 404 HTML). Only reachable internally at localhost:8001/health. Suggest also exposing /api/health.

The catch block still does `res.status(401).end()` without checking res.headersSent; if any future code sends a response before throwing this would re-throw ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT. Suggest `if (!res.headersSent) res.status(401).end();` and using 500 for genuine internal errors instead of 401.

action_items: None blocking - the fix (early `return` after res.status(401).end()) is verified working on the freshly restarted process.
Optional cleanup: delete the stray Redis key 'flw-txt-TEST_flw-txt-qa-invalid-sig' created by the pre-restart stale process.
Remember to restart the backend (ts-node, no hot reload) after every backend TS edit before self-verifying.
critical_code_review_comments: webhooks/index.ts flutterwaveWebHook: guard `if (!verifyFlutterwaveHash(signature)) { res.status(401).end(); return; }` is correct and fires before payload access (verified: malformed non-JSON body with bad hash now returns 401 with no 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading includes)' error, which the old code logged).
catch block should guard on res.headersSent and return 5xx for internal errors rather than masking them as 401.
verifyFlutterwaveHash correctly returns false for missing/empty header and uses constant-time comparison.
seed_data_creation: None. Only rejected (401) requests were sent; no users/payments/wallets created. One junk Redis key was written by the pre-restart stale process (see minor issues).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Webhook auth regression suite lives at /app/tests/test_flutterwave_webhook_auth.py (run: python -m pytest tests/test_flutterwave_webhook_auth.py). SAFETY: never send a valid verif-hash - this pod is on the LIVE PROD DB/Redis. Backend health only at http://localhost:8001/health (not public, not under /api). Backend is ts-node without hot reload -> restart backend after TS edits.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: missing `return` after res.status(401).end() let the handler continue to getRedisItem/setRedisItem on an unsigned payload and then res.status(200).end(). Verified reproduced on the stale process (webhookLogs showed processing of a 401'd payload) and verified fixed after restart (401 only, zero processing lines, zero headers-sent errors, /health still status=healthy database=connected).
